message:
fix(update): the optional images start after the commit, because before it they can close the way back

Relaunch was one step. It is two now: the host and the service, then
health, then the commit, and only then the client.

The client is started as the logged-on user, and when the route that
returns a handle is unavailable the shell starts it and returns nothing --
no handle, no way to say which process is ours, no way to stop it. A
rollback has to move the files such a process is holding. So starting the
client while a rollback is still possible risks closing the way back at
exactly the moment it is needed, and the previous behaviour proved it:
with the old order the scenario suite reports RollbackFailed and logs
"could not stop ScnClient.exe ... not rolling back".

Discovering the fall-through and reclassifying afterwards cannot fix that.
By the time it is discovered the process exists. The order removes the
situation instead of handling it.

The rollback path runs the same sequence -- restore, required, health,
optional -- so a client that will not come back cannot obscure whether the
restored host is up, or stand between the files and being put back.

RolledBackNotRelaunched now means the required images did not return after
a restore. It used to cover any relaunch failure, which called a window
that did not reopen by the same name as a machine nobody can reach; those
read very differently at three in the morning.

Two things surfaced while doing it. Clearing the outcome list per phase
looked tidier and dropped half the record, so a caller reading after both
phases indexed into an empty vector -- a real segfault, found only after
making that suite unbuffered, because the report died with the process
that was writing it. And the scenario harness had a knob that never fired:
nothing ever set rolledBack, so every restored build was judged by the new
build's health answer, and the cases asserting RestoredButUnhealthy were
passing for a reason they were not testing.
